decisions.id: D8a guard reach bounded to the clones directory

A worktree elsewhere is a scratch tree whose correct behavior is to be made and removed; refusing it would reach work the GM did not ask to stop (UNREQUESTED reach), and a hook cannot tell a scratch tree from a builder's except by where it lands. Taking the bound literally away would defeat no part of the request's purpose that the pool does not already serve.

decisions.id: L1 cp -a into the clones directory

The block's own goal (part A item 1, 'the only way to get a builder's tree is the pool') is contradicted by it. None of the three tests is met: it is not impossible to read a cp whose destination is a new directory directly under <mirror>/.clones/, nothing in the request implies it, and the literal reading defeats no stated purpose. A guard that passes bad work is a defect: either refuse it in T285 (same escape, red first), or carry it under 'Found and left?' with a filed task and its order, as T295 is carried.

decisions.id: L2 git clone into the clones directory

decisions.why: The block's own goal (Approach item 1) is a builder starting warm 'every time'; with the cache measured at over 150 GB against a 100 GB budget, the sweep is past its budget now, and idle pool trees - every free tree between builders - are what it evicts, so a free tree can be handed out with an emptied cache: the cold builder the task exists to end, left in place and not listed under 'Found and left?' (which reads 'none'; FR-009). decisions.summary: A free tree with uncommitted paths whose content is not HEAD's is refused for handout and names those paths. DISCARD=<reason> takes it over. Such a tree is never passed over for a new cold one.

decisions.summary: Release frees the tree and leaves the tree and its cache in place. make land and make land-batch call 'landed' after a landing, and a failed release never fails the landing.

decisions.summary: At every handout, a tree whose every holding task is ticked in tasks.md or archived in tasks-done.md is freed first, so a hand tick or a skipped release owes no hand step.
decisions.why: It closes the route by which a landing that skipped make land would leave a tree held and force a cold one. That is 'automatically ... performs the correct behavior'.

decisions.summary: 'A hold that names no feature is read by nothing there and waits for its release.' F= is optional on make builder-tree and on make builder-tree-adopt, so such holds arise from the pool's own advertised forms.
decisions.why: This is a carve-out from D6's own promise that 'no hand step is owed', and the block gives no reason for it. It leaves a route to the exact failure the GM named. A builder takes a tree with T= and no F=. Its task is then ticked by hand, or its landing's release does not run. The tree stays held for good, and the next take makes a new COLD tree while a reusable one sits idle. That is a wrong outcome (a cold builder, the tool answering wrongly), not a mere difference. Following the rule here is not physically impossible, the GM's words do not imply the exception, and following it does not defeat the request. Fix: make F= required on take and adopt (or derive it from the task's line in the clone's tasks.md, refusing when it cannot be found), so every hold is one D6's sweep reads. Pin the hand-tick case for that form in the any-route test.

decisions.why: Renaming would chill the caches, which is the failure being fixed. Membership is by registry, not by name shape, so the old names are full pool members. The figures carry a date and a method.

decisions.summary: The guard refuses git worktree add under <mirror>/.clones/, git worktree remove or move of a pool tree, and rm of a pool tree, its cache, or a directory holding either. Each refusal names the pool's command, and BUILDER_TREE_OK with a reason escapes.
decisions.why: This is the 'enforces ... without the opportunity for this kind of mistake' half. It refuses exactly the hand forms of 2026-11-26: a fresh tree made by hand, and a tree and cache deleted after a landing. move is refused because the measurement shows it chills the cache just as a removal does. decisions.summary: land-alone.sh, land-tooling.sh, review-tree.sh and the pool tool call git inside a program, so the hook never sees those calls. A hand 'git worktree add .../<clone>-land' is refused like any other, and the suite pins both cases.
decisions.why: The exemption is by call site, not by name, so no hand form escapes through a tooling tree's name. The call-site census states its search space (a grep of 'worktree add' over scripts/ and rust/).

decisions.summary: Refusal (a) reads only worktree-add targets under <mirror>/.clones/. Scratch worktrees elsewhere pass.
decisions.why: The trees the process rule and the pool define as builder trees live under the clones directory, and that is where the 2026-11-26 mistake was made. A worktree elsewhere is a scratch tree, not a builder tree made by mistake. Reaching one would mean a session relocating its tree after a refusal had named the pool, which is the same class as the recorded escape, not the inadvertent mistake the GM named. Recorded so a later round can check it: the dispatch and the brief are what put builders in pool trees, and nothing in this block checks a builder's tree outside .clones/.

decisions.summary: The shared walk reads git only by its bare name, so '/usr/bin/git worktree add ...' passes.
decisions.why: Not ruled as a legitimate exception: the block's stated reason, that every tree guard behaves this way, is consistency with existing code and could not legitimate a narrowing. It is within because it is not a route the GM's 'this kind of mistake' takes. The mistake was a session using the ordinary form, which is refused and pointed at the pool. Spelling out a path-qualified git is a deliberate bypass of the same class as the escape. A PreToolUse hook cannot see git called from inside a program anyway.

decisions.summary: A tree under the clones directory made by cp -a or git clone is not read.
decisions.why: The GM's words are 'whatever tooling we use to create worktrees'. A copy or a clone is not a worktree and is not how builder trees were or are made, so the request does not reach it.

decisions.summary: A new cold tree's cache is not seeded from a warm one.
decisions.why: Seeding is an optimization the request does not ask for. The request is that existing trees be reused and not deleted, and the pool makes a new tree only when every tree is held.

decisions.summary: The cache budget's eviction (evict.rs choose) skips a registered pool tree's build directory. The pool's share is bounded by cap x tree cache (about 40 GB, a GUESS from three measured sizes), shown by make builder-trees and returned by make builder-tree-drop.

First, applying the budget literally would defeat this request's purpose, as the block shows concretely: the cache was over its 100 GB budget at over 150 GB, a free pool tree ranks idle, so the sweep would empty it between builders and the next handout would be cold while called warm. Second, the GM's own words of 2026-11-22 imply it ('your points about reusing the same build cache and whatnot are well taken'). His concern then, space eaten 'without us realizing it', is answered by a bounded share that is priced, listed and reclaimable. Not confirmed from the block: whether T245's low-free-space automatic eviction also goes through choose and so skips pool trees, and whether make disk-audit names the pool's share. Neither blocks this ruling.

decisions.why: A builder tree made by hand under .clones/ is the GM's 'this kind of mistake' however git is spelled: it is just as cold, and the request is 'without the opportunity'. The reason given, that every tree guard shares the limit, is consistency with existing code, which is not a ground. It is not impossible (matching git by its basename in the walk is plainly doable). The GM's words do not imply it. Covering it would not defeat the request's purpose. The section also observed the guard passing this form (a check that passes bad work, a defect), deleted the test case that showed it, and records 'Found and left? none', so the defect is left without FR-009's why, filed task id and order. To clear it, preferably fix the walk (or the guard) so a path-qualified git is read and pin the case back in the suite. Otherwise carry it under 'Found and left?' as FR-009 requires: why it is not fixed here, a filed task id and 'lands before ...'.

decisions.summary: A tree under .clones/ made by cp -a or git clone is not a worktree and is not read by the guard.
decisions.why: The request is about the tooling that creates worktrees, and the mistake was a worktree. git clone under .clones/ is how clones themselves are made, so refusing it would block legitimate work. This is outside the request, not carved out of it.

decisions.why: Seeding was not asked for. The block's own rename measurement (fingerprints hold the absolute path) shows a copied cache would not be warm, so leaving it out loses nothing the request asked for.

decisions.id: D10 the cache budget never evicts a pool tree's build directory
decisions.summary: The sweep's choose skips a build directory named for a registered pool tree. The pool's share is bounded by cap times tree cache (about 40 GB GUESS, 174 GB free) and is given back only by builder-tree-drop.
decisions.why: This narrows T245's cache budget, whose 100 GB and idle-tree eviction are the session's design, not the GM's words. Applying the budget literally would defeat T285's purpose: it would empty each free pool tree between builders, so the next handout would be cold while called warm. The GM's own words of 2026-11-22 ('your points about reusing the same build cache and whatnot are well taken') support keeping the cache. His 'without us realizing it' still holds because the pool's share is bounded and visible in make builder-trees. Aside: the block does not say whether the low-free-space trigger shares choose. If it does, the pool is exempt there too, which is the same reasoning but worth one sentence in the block.

decisions.summary: make builder-tree hands out the task's tree, else the first free tree at HEAD, else ONE new cold tree under the cap with its guard binary built (1800 s GUESS knob); at the cap refused naming holders
decisions.why: the tooling performing the reuse ('automatically ... performs the correct behavior'); a cold tree is made only when no warm one exists, and is said to be cold

decisions.summary: a free tree with uncommitted content not in HEAD holds it: the handout is refused naming the paths, DISCARD with a reason takes it over; a held free tree is never passed over for a new cold one
decisions.why: refusing rather than making a cold tree past a warm one is the request's rule enforced, not narrowed; DISCARD is the project's reasoned, logged escape (FR-012's pattern)

decisions.summary: builder-tree-release and make land / land-batch free the tree and leave it and its cache in place; a release never fails a landing
decisions.why: the deletion after landing was the mistake; the landing now performs the correct step itself

decisions.summary: at every handout a tree whose holding tasks are ticked or archived is freed first
decisions.why: removes a hand step on which reuse would otherwise depend - 'without the opportunity for this kind of mistake'

decisions.id: D4c every hold names its feature
decisions.summary: a handout or adoption with a task and no feature is refused
decisions.why: makes D4b able to read every hold; serves the same clause

decisions.summary: make builder-trees lists; builder-tree-drop is the one removal (reason, logged, held tree refused); builder-tree-adopt joins a pre-pool worktree under its own name, the tooling's trees refused
decisions.why: drop is a deliberate, logged give-back of disk that the GM's disk words (2026-11-22, 2026-11-25) keep necessary, not the unthinking deletion after every landing; adopt keeps the three existing warm trees

decisions.id: D6 adopt by name, not rename
decisions.summary: the three trees of 2026-11-26 adopted under their names because a moved tree rebuilt every workspace crate (66.5 s / 41.7 s against 0.11 s / 0.08 s warm, measured 2026-11-26 with method)
decisions.why: the measured choice that keeps the caches warm, which is the request's purpose

decisions.summary: CAP = 4 (L7R_BUILDER_POOL), a GUESS knob from the sizing rule; T284 measures the count
decisions.why: a bound on the pool's size; refusing at the cap makes no hand route to a cold tree, and the request sets no count

decisions.id: D8a guard reach bounded to the clones directory
decisions.summary: the guard refuses `git worktree add` only for a path under <mirror>/.clones/; scratch worktrees elsewhere pass
decisions.why: Test: is the refused act a builder tree made by hand. The clones directory is where every builder tree lives (the pool's own trees, the hand trees of the mistake, -t269/-t270/-t271), so under it the guard reaches exactly the mistake's class. A worktree elsewhere is a scratch tree whose correct behavior is to be made and removed; refusing it would reach work the GM did not ask to stop (UNREQUESTED reach), and a hook cannot tell a scratch tree from a builder's except by where it lands. Taking the bound literally away would defeat no part of the request's purpose that the pool does not already serve.

decisions.summary: refuses worktree remove/move of a pool tree and rm of a pool tree, its cache or a directory holding either; BUILDER_TREE_OK with a reason escapes, checked first
decisions.why: the deletion half of the mistake, refused; move refused because it was measured to chill the cache; the reasoned escape is the accepted spec's guard pattern (FR-012)

decisions.id: D8c tooling trees exempt by call site
decisions.summary: land-alone.sh, land-tooling.sh, review-tree.sh and the pool tool call git inside a program, which a hook does not read; a hand `git worktree add .../<clone>-land` is refused
decisions.why: physically impossible otherwise: a PreToolUse hook reads only the tool call, not git calls inside a program; and these are the tooling the GM asked to perform the behavior, while the hand form of the same tree is still refused, so the exemption guts nothing

decisions.id: L1 cp -a into the clones directory
decisions.summary: a tree under the clones directory made by `cp -a` is not a worktree and not read (limit accepted)
decisions.why: Same test as D8a: under the clones directory any tree made by hand is a builder tree of the mistake's class, whatever command made it. 'Not a worktree' is the word-level argument; the purpose ('without the opportunity for this kind of mistake') is that no builder starts in a hand-made cold tree, and a copied tree is cold (the cache is keyed by the tree's name; D6 measured that a moved tree is not warm). The block's own goal (part A item 1, 'the only way to get a builder's tree is the pool') is contradicted by it. None of the three tests is met: it is not impossible to read a cp whose destination is a new directory directly under <mirror>/.clones/, nothing in the request implies it, and the literal reading defeats no stated purpose. A guard that passes bad work is a defect: either refuse it in T285 (same escape, red first), or carry it under 'Found and left?' with a filed task and its order, as T295 is carried.

decisions.id: L2 git clone into the clones directory
decisions.summary: a tree under the clones directory made by `git clone` is not a worktree and not read (limit accepted)
decisions.why: Judged on its own: a `git clone` to <mirror>/.clones/<name> handed to a builder is a fresh, cold, hand-made builder tree in the place builder trees live, which is the mistake the GM asked to have no opportunity for; the registry would not even hold it. The exemption rests on the word 'worktree', not on the request's purpose, and is not impossible to guard (a clone's destination under the clones directory is read from the command like a worktree's). Remedy as L1: refuse it in T285 with the same reasoned escape, or carry it as a filed defect with an order under FR-009's form.

decisions.id: L3 a new cold tree's cache not seeded
decisions.summary: a newly made pool tree's cache is not seeded from a warm one
decisions.why: not asked for; and the rename measurement (D6) shows a cache at a different absolute path rebuilds anyway, so seeding would not make a new tree warm

decisions.summary: /usr/bin/git worktree add passes the shared walk; filed as T295, fixed across every tree guard, lands before T284
decisions.why: a defect carried in FR-009's form: why not here (the shared walk every tree guard asks), filed id T295, order (lands before T284, the next work that relies on warm trees) - a scheduled fix, not a carve-out

decisions.id: D9c the budget never takes a pool tree's build directory
decisions.summary: the cache budget's eviction skips a registered pool tree's build directory; the pool's share is bounded by cap x tree cache (about 40 GB, GUESS) and given back by builder-tree-drop
decisions.why: a carve-out from the disk budget of T245, but implied by the GM's own words on the build caches (2026-11-22: 'your points about reusing the same build cache and whatnot are well taken'), and without it the sweep would empty every free pool tree between builders, defeating T285's purpose (handouts cold while called warm). The GM's disk concern ('without us realizing it') is met: the share is bounded and visible in make builder-trees, and drop returns it. Note for the builder: the block does not say whether the low-free-space trigger also skips pool trees; if it does, say so, since that is the place the GM asked for automatic action.
